1.note: V5 wins for clear, natural professional wording. All six omit Fuentes and Temuco, required by the Facts line even though absent from the original. V3 also switches from usted to tú and makes the four-week implementation approximate.

2.note: V5 wins for a concise follow-up that sounds natural in Chile. All versions omit the required Fuentes and Temuco. V3 additionally makes four weeks approximate, introduces an offer to adjust the proposal, and adds an overly familiar closing.

3.note: V2 wins: warm, conversational and complete. V3 and V6 are identical and equally good. V1 drops maintaining quality as the reason for the adjustment. V5 invents rent as the specific cost, adds having no alternative, switches the business voice to singular and promises to find a slot.

4.note: V1 wins by retaining an already natural message; V2, V4 and V5 are effectively tied with it. V3 introduces the minimizing description 'small adjustment.' V6 adds an unsupported claim that there is no alternative and a more distressed, emotionally dependent tone.

5.note: V4 wins for straightforward wording without unnecessary sales theatrics. V1 invents a half-afternoon schedule, repetitive emails and a specific editing workflow. V3 invents half-mornings, unanswered emails and a review workflow, while dropping the explicit minutes claim and professional-tone assurance.

6.note: V2 wins for natural Chilean phrasing and a clean explanation. None explicitly mentions the reel required by the Facts line. V3 invents habitual difficulty, a drafting workflow and half-mornings lost. V6 also invents personal history and a workflow, and drops the explicit assurance about preserving the author's tone.

7.note: V4 wins for preserving the story while reducing formulaic presentation. V1 invents rising sales and pricing struggles, changes an imperfect website to an unfinished one, and loses the freedom lesson. V5 exaggerates frequency, adds an ego admission, changes unpublished success stories to none, and narrows financing to credit.

8.note: V6 wins for fluent, faithful prose. V4 adds organizational struggles, work already underway and a new admission about not knowing how things will go. V5 invents an exact departure date and personal feelings, implies the bank failed to teach business skills, and changes the closing question from difficulty to postponement.

9.note: V5 wins for keeping the family history and working commitments in plain prose. V1 invents customers bringing their families and adds boastful slogans. V2 invents the father's instruction of the current team and customer recommendations, while dropping the explicit commitment to avoid repeat repairs. All retain the core Facts.

10.note: V3 wins by making small, natural improvements to an already usable original. V1 is equally strong. V2 invents repair-priority advice, price explanations and a guarantee that customers will always see the same staff. The other versions preserve the facts without material additions.

11.note: V5 wins for clear, appropriately professional language. All still need their placeholders completed. V2 adds next-day usability and an exaggerated claim about technological change. V3 adds specific privacy, authorship and review content. V6 inserts an unsolicited definition and drops explicit coverage of classroom implications; its experience claim remains a labeled example.

12.note: V6 wins for concise, clear proposal language with every required fact intact. No version materially changes the price, participants or schedule. V1 and V5 lightly reinterpret the pedagogical aims. V4 is less polished and shifts from describing the program's aim to an expectation of what teachers should know afterward.

13.note: V5 wins for warmth and retention of the standing welcome. All remove the original 'best view' claim; V1 and V3 also remove the always-available-place assurance. V4 invents the guest enjoying sunset and changes pride to uncertainty about the recommendations. V6 loses the explicit terrace view, assumes the tips proved useful and promises a ready terrace.

14.note: V3 wins for a minimal, conversational edit. V5 and V6 are identical. None identifies the business as a hostal, required by the Facts line but absent from the original. V1 adds Marcela's predicted reaction and assumes the advice was useful. V4 also adds her reaction and drops the explicit view.

15.note: V5 narrowly wins for faithful, readable copy, but the retained claim that November starts the cold season is unsuitable for Chile. V1, V2 and V6 retain it too. V3 removes it but invents readers recommending the shop and staying to chat, and drops the Zambra appraisal. V4 asserts cooling has already begun and changes that appraisal.

16.note: V4 wins for clear, friendly wording that preserves the information and invitation. V1, V3, V5 and V6 keep the substantive facts, with minor shifts in enthusiasm or audience framing. V2 adds a promise to help choose books and an anticipation backstory; 'te apetece' also feels less local.

17.note: V1 wins for direct, natural wording that preserves the firm deadline and willingness to discuss a problem. V3 is equally sound. V4 drops the explicit second-payment identification and softens the transfer question. V2 introduces speculation, an unauthorized 'no problem' concession and an overly affectionate closing.
